newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China to deliver copper to Singapore LME store.
newsitem.headline: China to deliver copper to Singapore LME store.

text.p: China will deliver between 8,000 to 10,000 tonnes of copper to the London Metal Exchange (LME) warehouse in Singapore over the next month, a Chinese industry official said on Tuesday.

"We know between 8,000 to 10,000 tonnes will be delivered to the Singapore warehouse of the LME because the domestic price is very low and the international market price hit US$2,600 a tonne," the official from the China National Nonferrous Metals Import and Export Corp (CNIEC) said.
He was speaking to Reuters at the Asia Copper Forum '97 conference in Singapore.
The Far East base metal trade has been swirling with reports about the volume of copper China will sell to take advantage of current high prices on the LME.
Three month copper was quoted by regional dealers at 0640 GMT at US$2,595/600 a tonne compared with the late quote in London on Monday of $2,597 a tonne.
The CNIEC official said the copper will be shipped "between now to July from Shanghai and Canton."
The volume of copper in the LME's Singapore warehouse reached 16,950 tonnes on Monday, down 1,100 tonnes from the previous day's level.

Asked if China will transport more copper to the LME warehouse in the city-state over the next few weeks, the CNIEC official said: "I don't know about that. The price and also the domestic demand is the chief consideration."
China prohibits exports of copper that is produced domestically because of shortages of the metal.
Copper imports in 1996 hit around 851,700 tonnes compared with 601,700 tonnes the previous year, Chinese custom statistics showed.
